subject: Runway stall: remediation proposal, MAP rebaseline & request for escalation
messages:
From: Leah Martinez <leah.m@orionhealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan timing questions / procurement window

Hi Olga,

Quick note on timing — procurement has flagged a hit to our September acceptance window. Our legal team asked to push the PO review by two weeks because of recent internal audits; that moves the internal approval to the week of Oct 4, which in turn shifts our final acceptance target.

Can Redwood confirm whether a two-week MAP rebaseline would require any changes to the quoted onboarding SLO or the proposed cutover slices? Ben, looping you for the updated impacts to delivery and pricing.

We attached the procurement timeline for reference (Orion_RFP_schedule.xlsx). If we need to lock an alternate acceptance lane to preserve our go-live for the product showcase on Oct 21, please advise.

Thanks,
Leah Martinez
Sr. Procurement Manager
Orion Health

Attachment: Orion_RFP_schedule.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Leah Martinez <leah.m@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan timing questions / procurement window

Leah — thanks for the heads up and for sending the timeline.

Short answer: we can absorb a two-week slip without changing the core onboarding scope, but it will change the schedule for our phased validation windows unless we take one of two actions:

1) Hold the originally proposed canary cutover (Oct 14) and accept a compressed eval window (shorter validation cycles, higher risk).
2) Rebaseline the MAP and move the cutover + acceptance lanes two weeks later, which preserves test coverage but delays the Oct 21 showcase by one week.

I'll let Ben outline the operational impacts (autoscaling warm-up, dedicated capacity reservation) and any pricing implications. Can you confirm whether your legal team can commit to a firm sign-off date in the Oct 4–8 range? That will determine the path we recommend.

If helpful, I can draft a short MAP amendment that documents the rebaseline and acceptance criteria — that would make it easier for your procurement/legal to sign.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0173
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Leah Martinez <leah.m@orionhealth.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Mutual action plan timing questions / procurement window

Thanks for looping me in. Technical/contractual impact summary below so the decision is clear for procurement/legal: 

- Two-week rebaseline (preferred: Oct 4 sign-off) — Operational impact: minimal change to total engineering effort; we keep the same number of validation cycles. Commercial impact: none for list price if commitment stays the same.
- If Orion needs the Oct 21 showcase preserved and we compress validation: operational risk increases for cutover (estimated +12% probability of a post-cutover ticket within 30 days). To preserve showcase we can offer a one-time technical support window the week following cutover at no charge, but that requires an executive-level sign-off on a temporary SLA exception.

Attached is a proposed MAP amendment (proposed-rebaseline-MAP_v1.pdf) that documents both options and the acceptance criteria for each. Olga — I marked the places where we'd need a signature and where we might require the SLA exception checkbox.

Leah — which route would you prefer us to prepare for? If you want option 2 (preserve Oct 21), we'll start working the exception paperwork and prep the staging runs to fit the compressed window. If option 1, we'll prepare the rebaseline amendment for your sign-off and update the Dedicated capacity reservations to match the shifted cadence.

Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Exec, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0104

Attachment: proposed-rebaseline-MAP_v1.pdf (PDF, 78KB)

Leah — following up after our internal sync. We discussed both paths with Solutions and Sales and want to be explicit about the operational tradeoffs so procurement can make a clean choice.

Summary of asks from Redwood: 
- If Orion selects the two-week rebaseline (preferred): please confirm firm sign-off window of Oct 4–8 in writing. We will update the MAP and issue an amended acceptance schedule; no pricing changes.
- If Orion needs the Oct 21 showcase preserved: please confirm by EOD Sep 30 so we can: 1) provision a temporary support window for Oct 22–28, and 2) request a short SLA exception from our ops leadership (Ben, please route to your escalation channel). There is no automatic cost, but the exception requires executive approval.

We are prepared to attach the MAP amendment to the existing SOW and move quickly once you confirm the desired path. I have drafted the amendment language and uploaded it to our shared drive (link below).
